text:
eli: quick proposal: a decision-ladder approach for model rollouts instead of fixed-stepped canaries. short version: dynamic step sizes based on traffic sensitivity + guard tiers, with automated backoff and explicit holdpoints.

sam: love the name. what do you mean by "dynamic step sizes"?

eli: think of it as a ladder where rungs are percent targets but the size between rungs can adapt. e.g. initial micro-rungs (0.5%, 1%, 2%) for high-sensitivity customers, then wider rungs (5%, 10%, 25%) once metrics are stable.

marta: how would we express that in the rollout API? can we keep it compatible with existing staged-ramp fields?

eli: propose a minimal schema addition: rollout.ladder = [{"target_pct":"0.5","min_duration":"10m","guard":"tierA"}, {"target_pct":"1","min_duration":"10m","guard":"tierA"}, ...]

ryan: pls avoid nested json in slack msg :grin: but i get it. key question: what are guard tiers?

eli: good call — guard tiers map to sets of telemetry checks. tierA = strict (p95 latency, error-rate, model-quality eval on control prompts); tierB = standard (error-rate + SLO slides). ladder rungs reference a guard name.

anya: how do we compute "model-quality eval" live? that used to be slow.

marta: we can run a sampled evaler: mirror X% of requests to the new model and run lightweight heuristics + a small eval corpus each rung. result is a single metric: quality_delta_pct.

sam: what's the abort threshold? also need to avoid noisy aborts from tiny sample sizes.

eli: defaults: abort if error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute OR p95 latency increase > 20% OR quality_delta_pct <= -1.0 with 95% bootstrap CI excluding 0. We also require min_samples per rung (e.g. 2000 requests) before evaluating quality.

ryan: robust. add a rolling CI check helps. what about traffic-sensitive tenants? they'd blow past micro-rungs if we wait for samples.

eli: ladder supports cohort pinning. you can mark rungs as cohort-only (e.g. internal/trial customers) and specify quota-aware targets. Also a "fast-pass" flag for low-risk models that fast-tracks after tierA identical metrics for 2 consecutive rungs.

anya: console UX: how do we show this? I want a timeline with annotated holdpoints and a live "risk score" per rung.

marta: agree — in the rollout UI we can show current rung, time left, sample count, and each guard's status (green/yellow/red). clicking a guard opens a telemetry drilldown (p95 trend, error histogram, quality examples).

sam: API debate: should gradual rollouts be expressed as an ordered list of steps or as this ladder object? backwards compat matters.

eli: implement ladder as a superset. if user passes legacy steps array, we convert to ladder with static guard references. new ladder lets dynamic spacing.

ryan: what about A/B experiments where we want two new variants simultaneously (split 5/5 vs baseline)?

eli: ladder supports multi-variant rungs. each rung can carry a list of variants + their target fractions. e.g. rung1: [{v2:2},{v3:2}] total=4 -> normalized. The same guards apply across variants.

anya: telemetry hooks: we'll need to emit events at rung transitions and on guard breaches. format: rollout.event {rung, variant, metric, value, reason}. these feed console + alerts.

marta: console should have quick-action buttons: pause, rollback-to-last-stable, inject-more-traffic (manual override). also an "emergency abort" that applies immediately across all variants.

sam: how do we handle capacity/backpressure? if new model requires more memory/gpu and latency increases due to queuing, we need to auto-reduce target.

eli: include a capacity-sensitivity guard that watches queue-depth and compute throughput per-slot. if throughput drops > X% we back off a rung and re-evaluate with reduced percent. also mark that rollout as "capacity-limited" in UI.

ryan: sounds like a lot of knobs — what are sane defaults for teams who don't want to tune?

eli: default ladder: [0.5% (10m, tierA), 1% (10m, tierA), 2% (15m, tierB), 5% (30m, tierB), 10% (1h, tierB), 25% (2h, tierC), 50% (4h, tierC), 100% (manual finalize)]. default guards: error delta 0.5%, p95 +20%, quality -1% with min_samples=2000. default backoff: step back 1 rung and pause for 15m.

marta: telemetry cost: sample evals + mirror traffic increase token usage. we should add quota-aware behavior: if customer's remaining quota < threshold, we restrict eval mirroring frequency and fall back to synthetic evals. document this in Console help.

anya: alerting integration: send a short escalation if guard breaches twice in a 1h window. integration with oncall routing.

sam: edge case: model family multimodal where some inputs are heavy. suggest per-route override for ladder (so image-heavy endpoints use more conservative ladder).

eli: yes — ladder can be scoped per-route or global. route-scoped ladders inherit defaults. good call.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by eli at 1749007654 for rollout "ladder-experiment-3" -> state: rung_0 (0.5%) started

marta: can we log a reproducible snapshot of the model binary + quantization profile per rung so rollback is exact?

eli: absolutely — each rung stores model_hash, quant_profile, and infra snapshot. rollback uses those.

ryan: next steps: I'll sketch API backward-compatible patch, marta can mock up console, anya will wire telemetry events. We should get a quick internal beta with canary-only scope (internal customers) before exposing.

sam: +1. timeline?

eli: propose 2-week sprint for API + backend checks, 1 week for console mock, then internal beta. I'll post a design doc with examples and the minimal schema.

marta: leaving notes for UX: show CI band for quality metric, sample counts, and a single-click revert.

anya: I'll create event specs and sample payloads for each guard breach.

sam: thanks all.

eli: thanks — filing design doc now: https://redwood.internal/docs/rollouts/decision-ladder-draft (will update with API examples)
